headline: No dip on the board: BTC $84.0k mid-range, 10y 5.16%, Oct hike odds near 70%
summary: At 09:54 UTC on Saturday 26 September the tape is quiet and mildly heavy, with no dip trigger anywhere: BTC is $83,996.10 against an $84,090.50 open (-0.11%), sitting 40% up an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band, ETH is $2,681.08 (-0.38%) and still the laggard at 17% of a $2,668.33-$2,742.42 range, and SOL is $119.89 (-1.83%), the only one really moving after closing Friday +4.27% at $122.01. Weekly changes are +3.6% BTC, +1.7% ETH, +7.6% SOL, and SOL's intraday flush to $117.90 (-4.1% from its $122.91 high) was already bought back to $119.89 - give-back after a rally, not panic. Two things changed since the last briefing. Bitget's staged withdrawal restart is now confirmed and dated - BTC from 28 September 08:00 UTC, ETH the 29th, USDT the 30th, everything else 2 October - with the $387.5m loss covered by a protection fund holding over $464m and Mandiant and SlowMist on the investigation, so the acute wound now has a timetable rather than an open question. And Friday's 08:00 UTC quarterly settlement cleared roughly $15.9bn of bitcoin options plus $2.1bn of ether on Deribit, 37% of Deribit's $43.5bn bitcoin open interest, which switched off the dealer hedging that had been pinning price near the $85,000 strike; the range is now held by spot flows and the bond market alone. Macro is still the cap: the US 10-year finished Friday around 5.163%, just off Thursday's 5.205% high since June 2007, and markets price 64-70% odds of a further 25bp hike at the 27-28 October FOMC after a 58.4 S&P Global composite PMI. Fear & Greed is 74 and the composite reads 65.1, both Greed, on 66 items in 24 hours - half the prior flow - with Hyperliquid funding uniformly mild at 0.00125%/h across all three, futures at a small discount to spot (-0.045% BTC, -0.039% SOL, -0.012% ETH) and SOL open interest edging down to $677.8m: a de-levered, un-crowded weekend book with nothing to buy.

BTC.note: $83,996.10, down 0.11% on the session and 40% up an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band on $3.17bn of open interest, funding of 0.00125%/h and a -0.045% futures discount to spot - range consolidation with no crowded long and no dip to buy.

ETH.note: $2,681.08, off 0.38% and again the weakest of the three at 17% of a $2,668.33-$2,742.42 range and only +1.7% on the week, on $2.94bn of open interest and a -0.012% premium - drifting toward the low end of its band without any seller urgency behind it.

SOL.note: $119.89, down 1.83% and 2.5% off its $122.91 high after a Friday close of $122.01 (+4.27%); the intraday flush to $117.90 was recovered within the session, it is still +7.6% on the week and 40% up its range, and open interest has eased to $677.8m - an orderly unwind of a rally, not a panic flush.

drivers.title: Friday's $15.9bn options expiry removed the dealer hedging that pinned the range
drivers.detail: Roughly $15.9bn of bitcoin options and $2.1bn of ether options settled on Deribit at 08:00 UTC on Friday 25 September, between 167,000 and 184,000 bitcoin contracts (106,200 calls, 75,900 puts) and 37% of Deribit's $43.5bn bitcoin open interest, with max pain at $75,000-$76,000, more than $8,000 below spot at settlement. The mechanical hedging that had been holding price near the $85,000 strike is switched off, so from here the range is held only by spot flows and macro - the first weekend in a month without that dampener, on a book where funding is a uniform 0.00125%/h and all three futures trade at a discount to spot.

drivers.title: 10-year at ~5.163% and 64-70% odds of an October hike still cap the range
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield finished Friday 25 September at about 5.163%, essentially unchanged on the day but only just off Thursday's 5.205%, the highest since June 2007, after hawkish remarks from Fed Governor Michael Barr that "further policy adjustments" should be expected. CME FedWatch puts a further 25bp hike at the 27-28 October FOMC near 64%, with other venues 67-70%, helped by a S&P Global composite PMI of 58.4 on Wednesday, the strongest in more than five years. CoinDesk noted on 25 September that bond volatility has surged while bitcoin and equities stayed calm - the divergence is what would close violently if yields break higher.

drivers.title: Bitget restart confirmed and dated: BTC withdrawals 28 Sept 08:00 UTC
drivers.detail: Bitget has confirmed a staged restart after the $387.5m drain (initially estimated $351.6m, raised once Zcash and TRON transfers were traced): Bitcoin withdrawals resume 28 September at 08:00 UTC, ETH on Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base and Optimism on the 29th, USDT on Ethereum, BSC, Solana and TRON on the 30th, and other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October, all at 08:00 UTC. The exchange says the vulnerability is patched, Mandiant and SlowMist are investigating, user balances are unchanged and the loss sits inside a protection fund holding more than $464m; trading and deposits never stopped. Circle and Tether froze only about $318,000, while roughly 67,982 ETH (~$183m) was swapped and remains unfrozen.

drivers.title: ETF streak holds at seven days but the size is 81% off the week's peak
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs took $134.46m on 25 September for a seventh consecutive inflow day - IBIT +$96.99m and FBTC +$49.32m against BITB -$11.85m - but that is 81% below Monday's $999m, the largest single day of 2026, so the institutional bid is intact in direction and decaying in size. Note the venues disagree on the number: SatsIntel put the same day's aggregate at +$37.5m, so treat the level as provisional. Separately Strategy is asking shareholders to approve daily accrual of preferred dividends to pull STRC back toward $100, after putting $174.0m into repurchasing its own preferred versus $75.7m into bitcoin in the 14-20 September week.

drivers.title: Trump-Xi state visit ends with the trade truce pushed to 10 January 2027
drivers.detail: The White House published its fact sheet and closing release on the Xi Jinping state visit (23-25 September) on 26 September, and Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed the year-old trade truce is extended two months, from 10 November to 10 January 2027, with China committing to 25m metric tons of US soybeans a year through 2028. Coverage describes the visit as spectacle over substance with few concrete deliverables, but the practical effect for risk assets is that the tariff cliff is off the calendar until January - one fewer scheduled shock between now and the October FOMC.

drivers.title: Regulatory drip continues: Peirce out 2 Oct, CFTC sues Cash FX, EU flags quantum risk
drivers.detail: Cointelegraph confirmed at 09:02 UTC today that SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, who ran the agency's Crypto Task Force, leaves on 2 October, cutting the SEC to Chair Atkins and Mark Uyeda after the Senate's CLARITY Act cloture vote failed and the Blockchain Association's CFTC-veteran leader also departed. The CFTC has sued Cash FX over an alleged $950m crypto-linked forex scheme, and the EU's Joint Committee of supervisory authorities used its Autumn 2026 Risk and Vulnerabilities report (24 September) to warn that quantum attacks could arrive before commercial quantum viability, putting roughly 6.9m BTC - about $586bn at current prices - held in old or reused addresses at eventual risk. None of this is a near-term price driver, but it is a steady one-way drift in US policy support.

watch.what: Bitget reopens Bitcoin withdrawals, the first of four stages. Withdrawals stay frozen until then, so this is where the story either closes cleanly or slips a second time - the loss estimate already moved from $351.6m to $387.5m once. A queue that clears quietly removes the last acute crypto risk; a delay is the single most likely source of a genuine panic flush this week.

The rest of the Bitget restart, each stage at 08:00 UTC: ETH on the 29th, USDT on the 30th, other tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October. The USDT stage on the 30th is the one that would show up in stablecoin pricing if any stage goes badly.

Falcon Finance (FF) one-year lock-up expiry releases 203,055,556 tokens in four tranches, about 6.47% of circulating supply and roughly $27.1m. Small in absolute terms and not a BTC/ETH/SOL event, but it starts a dense October unlock calendar that runs through Sui, Arbitrum, Starknet, Aptos and Jito.

Quarter-end data cluster: US personal income and outlays with the PCE deflator, ADP private payrolls (consensus +70k), the final Q2 GDP estimate, JOLTS openings (7.23m expected from 7.27m), plus Chinese PMIs and flash euro-zone CPI. With October hike odds at 64-70% and the 10-year at a 19-year high, a firm PCE is the most direct scheduled pressure on the yield that is capping this range.
ISM Manufacturing PMI and weekly jobless claims, read as the warm-up to Friday's payrolls after Wednesday's 58.4 composite PMI already pushed hike odds up.

September employment report (08:30 ET): consensus about +100k nonfarm payrolls from +162k, unemployment ticking to 4.2% from 4.1%, average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m and 3.2% y/y. A hot print into a Fed already 64-70% priced to hike is the clearest route to a macro-driven dip; the same day is Hester Peirce's last at the SEC.

US-Iran technical contacts on a phased Strait of Hormuz reopening, against the seven-day timeline Iranian foreign minister Araghchi set out on Friday. Progress is the cleanest route to lower oil and lower yields; a repeat of the June 17 memorandum collapsing puts the 10-year back at 5.205% and BTC back toward $83,163.

FOMC rate decision (2:00 p.m. ET, meeting 27-28 October), currently 64-70% priced for a further 25bp hike. The US-China truce now runs to 10 January 2027, so tariffs are not competing for attention before then.
